result.title: Offline Makes Online Better: Calibrated Cache Compression for Video Generation
result.summary: Token merging is an effective approach to reducing KV-cache memory consumption in autoregressive video generation by clustering temporally redundant tokens and retaining only a small set of representatives. Existing methods, however, typically apply a uniform merging ratio across all attention layers and heads. We observe that different layers and heads exhibit substantially different yet jointly correlated sensitivities to token merging, and that these sensitivity patterns remain consistent across prompts. Based on this observation, we introduce CALM, a Calibrated Allocation for Layer-Head Merging that uses offline calibration to improve online cache compression. Exhaustively evaluating all possible layer-head allocations is prohibitively expensive. To enable efficient calibration, we show that attention-output error strongly correlates with end-to-end video quality and can therefore serve as a lightweight proxy for allocation risk assessment. We evaluate different allocation strategies using this proxy and construct a fixed layer-head risk map offline. Given a cache budget at inference time, CALM uses dynamic programming to determine the best allocation of merging ratios. Experiments across three different autoregressive video models demonstrate that CALM consistently outperforms uniform token merging under the same memory budget, by reducing the LPIPS to original videos by around 21% with higher video-quality scores.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CALM：先离线校准各层各头对 token 合并的敏感度，以注意力输出误差作为画质代理构建风险图，推理时用动态规划在固定缓存预算下分配层-头合并比例，用于自回归视频生成的 KV-cache 压缩。
AI.relevance_reason: 层-头敏感度差异、离线校准与误差代理可能为 LVR 中按层分配视觉细节保留或压缩预算、以及缓存结构对 latent 状态的影响提供核查线索，但研究对象是视频生成，迁移性有待验证。
